log.msg: The burial: rail() renders usage → compose → effort_groups, and effort_groups sorts efforts by their liveliest task but never lifts running tasks OUT of their group — a running task sits wherever its effort landed in the list, below every idea in a livelier group. The order is fine inside a group; there is just no ACROSS-group view of what is running.

Design: active_strip() lands in dashboard.js, not a new file — it needs load()/active()/state()/card(), all module-private there, and a sibling active.js importing load() while dashboard.js imports the strip is the mutual-import trap. Zero new CSS: the strip is .ai-group + .ai-group-title + .ai-cards + card(t, true), the same vocabulary the groups below use. Mike is complaining about ORDER, not looks.

action.note: active_strip() + strip() in dashboard.js, called first inside rail(); index prose now says Active first. Zero CSS.

log.msg: Verified with global playwright at 400/1280/1920/3440: .ai-active is the rail's first child at every width, 3 running cards (board-active-first, mirror-root-fix, panel-review — wire-reference correctly absent, it landed at 20:33), .ai-cards gives 1/1/2/3 columns, doc scrollWidth overflow 0, zero console errors. The one thing the strip cannot do: a task that STARTS while the board is open still needs a reload, because enumeration is directory.json and only logs already on the board stream. Same hole as the day dashboard — ranked #1 in doc/file/dashboard.js.md.

assign.outcome: **Active strip at the top of `/framework/ai/`.** `active_strip()` (dashboard.js) pins every task with `requested_at` and no `landed_at`, newest first, across every day — the same `card()` the rail already uses, above the usage meters, the compose box and the effort groups (which stay, and stay grouped). Those few logs re-`load()` through `live()`, so their bars and `now` lines move in place and a task that lands drops out of the strip with no reload; `all_tasks()` below stays a plain fetch. **Zero new CSS** — the strip is `.ai-group` + `.ai-cards` + `.ai-card`, so it inherits the responsive card grid (1 column at 400, 3 at 3440).
